markdown_report:
The best next experiment is a controlled increase in endpoint supervision within each category’s single BERT4Rec model. At 10% research progress, a small objective change is more informative than architectural expansion; no validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Appended-mask inference has no right context, whereas interior reconstruction can use future interactions. Endpoint supervision therefore tests an identifiable training–inference discrepancy. (2) Equal group weights can reproduce the existing objective exactly. Baseline reduction and realized group counts must be established before spending training budget. (3) Electronics has a 13.6% diagnostic wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-tail margin. This identifies a training-probe weakness, but neither explains its cause nor establishes validation performance.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec [1] establishes masked reconstruction, and DualRec [2] discusses past–future context discrepancy. Their connection motivates a supervision intervention without importing dual networks. (2) Embedding-collapse research [3] motivates spectrum measurements beyond mean cosine. Electronics’ directional similarity alone cannot establish collapse or recommendation diversity. (3) Sampling research [4] questions agreement between sampled and full-catalog rankings. Diagnostic margins therefore cannot replace the pinned host metric.

**Framework and directions.** Three directions separate intervention from measurement:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed extension | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supervision | Interior and endpoint masking | Explicit endpoint weight | Host validation determines benefit |
| Context dependence | Bidirectional reconstruction | Matched prefix/interior probe | Dependence is not user preference |
| Representation | Mean embedding cosine | Effective-rank probe | Geometry is not ranking quality |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Endpoint weight 0.75 — 3/6/3.** Positive: simple, interpretable alignment experiment. Negative: heuristic and closely related to existing masking objectives.
- **Matched context-gap probe — 4/6/4.** Positive: distinguishes right-context dependence using identical targets. Negative: positional controls complicate interpretation; the probe itself does not improve ranking.
- **Effective-rank diagnostic — 2/4/2.** Positive: complements cosine with dimensional concentration. Negative: cannot establish a useful training intervention.

**Selected experiment.** Compare the exact supplied baseline with a weight-only candidate, using endpoint weight 0.75 and reconstruction weight 0.25. Preserve the baseline’s within-group reduction, loss, sampling, masks and total batch size. If constructing these groups changes the baseline, require a matched-construction control; per-example normalization remains a separate ablation. Equal-weight 0.5 is unnecessary when algebraically identical to the control.

```text
record exact baseline objective and group construction
draw identical seeded prefixes and corruption masks across arms
replace every supervised input target with reserved MASK
E, R = baseline_within_group_losses(model, batch)
loss = exact_baseline_reduce(E, R) or .75*E + .25*R
backward once; update the single model
```

Keep all four categories, fixed seeds, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Preserve appended-mask inference, final-nonpadding readout, predictor/checkpoint consistency and diagnostic interfaces. Budget controls and diagnostics within 43,200 GPU-seconds; select exclusively by host macro validation HR@10. Titles cannot establish ownership, compatibility or immediate need.

References: [1] BERT4Rec; [2] DualRec; [3] Guo et al., ICML 2024; [4] sampling reliability, RecSys 2025. Links appear below.

idea.description: Test a fixed endpoint-supervision weight of 0.75 against the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, retaining one independently trained model per category. Combine endpoint and ordinary reconstruction losses in one optimizer update while preserving each group’s original loss reduction.
idea.motivation: Endpoint masking matches the absence of right context at appended-mask inference. The supplied diagnostic shows weaker training separation for Electronics, but does not demonstrate that context mismatch causes that weakness. A controlled weight change tests this hypothesis without changing the backbone or introducing independent predictors.
idea.implementation_notes: First document the supplied baseline’s precise loss, reduction, group construction and masking policy; these are not provided here. Omit algebraically duplicate comparisons. If endpoint/reconstruction group construction differs from the baseline, retain the exact baseline and require a matched-construction control before attributing differences to weighting. Do not introduce per-example normalization in the weight-only experiment. Use identical seeded sampling streams across comparison arms and clean preceding context for endpoint examples. Every supervised target must be replaced by the reserved MASK token, with labels used only in the loss. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Keep execution single-GPU and allocate all comparison training, diagnosis and failures within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Each deployed category loads exactly one checkpoint; no averaging or score fusion. Preserve the predictor writer and appended-mask inference with final-nonpadding readout. Keep ModelView hooks, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Report measured group losses and target counts as diagnostics, not replacements for host macro validation HR@10. Do not access test files, other trials, unavailable metadata or pretrained downloads. No empirical improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
spec = document_corrected_baseline_objective()
assert comparison_is_nonredundant(spec, endpoint_weight=0.75)
# If constructing groups changes sampling, add a matched-construction control.
for category in four_categories:
    model = initialize_corrected_bert4rec(seed=42)
    for epoch in range(at_most_200):
        for step in range(200):
            enforce_predeclared_gpu_time_budget()
            groups = draw_seeded_baseline_compatible_groups()
            assert_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK(groups)
            endpoint_loss = spec.reduce_within_group(loss_terms(model, groups.endpoint))
            reconstruction_loss = spec.reduce_within_group(loss_terms(model, groups.reconstruction))
            loss = 0.75 * endpoint_loss + 0.25 * reconstruction_loss
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
    save_one_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(category, model)
# Inference: retain history with room for appended MASK, left-pad,
# encode bidirectionally, and read the final nonpadding position.
# Select the configuration using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Explicit objective accounting makes the supervision-allocation hypothesis testable while separating it from normalization and sampling changes.
originality.negative: Endpoint masking and weighted multitask objectives are established; the proposed coefficient is heuristic.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could motivate subsequent studies of context mismatch and supervision schedules within a single model.
future_potential.negative: A gain may be benchmark-specific, and repeated validation search cannot establish generalization across seeds or datasets.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention changes two loss coefficients and leaves inference architecture intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducing baseline reductions and controlling sampled groups requires care; missing baseline source prevents a concrete implementation here.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item inference.
Provides the backbone and supervision mechanisms retained in the proposed experiment.
limitations: Interior reconstruction can use right context unavailable at next-item inference.
Does not establish that the proposed 0.75 supervision weight improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: Disentangling Past-Future Modeling in Sequential Recommendation via Dual Networks
contributions: Identifies discrepancies between past-context prediction and modeling that uses future context.
limitations: Its dual-network solution is excluded from this proposal under the task’s single-model requirement.
Its motivation does not validate a particular endpoint-loss coefficient.

related_work.title: ICML 2024 study of embedding collapse in recommendation
contributions: Motivates examining low-rank embedding structure beyond average pairwise cosine similarity.
limitations: Embedding geometry alone does not establish recommendation quality or diversity.
The supplied cosine measurements do not demonstrate low-rank collapse.

related_work.title: RecSys 2025 study of sampling reliability in recommendation evaluation
contributions: Examines reliability of sampled recommendation evaluation and its agreement with fuller evaluation settings.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.
Single-negative training margins remain distinct from the benchmark’s 100-candidate HR@10.
